name: LLM.int8(): 8-bit Matrix Multiplication for Transformers at Scale
problem: INT8 quantization of LLMs fails because a tiny set of emergent outlier feature dimensions dominates attention output and destroys the quantization error budget.
mechanism: Two-part mixed-precision decomposition: (1) vector-wise quantization - each inner product in the matmul keeps its own normalization constant computed over the row of activations, instead of one per-tensor scale; (2) mixed-precision decomposition - outlier feature dimensions (columns with large systematic magnitude) are extracted into a small 16-bit matmul whose partial products are summed separately, so >99.9% of values still multiply in 8-bit. Keeps the outliers out of the INT8 GEMM entirely rather than widening it.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): halves inference memory vs 16/32-bit while 'retaining full precision performance'; a 175B-parameter 16/32-bit checkpoint loads, converts to INT8 and runs with no performance degradation; >99.9% of multiplications occur in 8-bit. COMPRESSION RATIO: 2x weight memory (16-bit -> 8-bit). QUALITY COST: stated as zero ('without any performance degradation') - this is a self-reported claim against OPT/BLOOM zero-shot suites, not an independent measurement.
